# A test program that goes away in the middle of its run fails it.
#
# A Go target's test runs in a program of its own, and a stack overflow ends
# that program where no recover reaches. The driver read the end of its
# output as the end of a run and printed `ok 0 tests`, which a script's
# `stdout ok` accepted. The test that was running now fails, naming the exit,
# and is recorded as any failure is. The interpreter, html and android report
# the overflow as the test's failure themselves.

! sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'not ok +2 tests, 1 failures'
! sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'not ok +2 tests, 1 failures'
! sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'not ok +2 tests, 1 failures'
stdout 'the test program exited during TheProgramGoesAway'
! sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'not ok +2 tests, 1 failures'
stdout 'the test program exited during TheProgramGoesAway'
! sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'not ok +2 tests, 1 failures'
stdout 'the test program exited during TheProgramGoesAway'
! sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'not ok +2 tests, 1 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

// Counts down from n, one call per step: a deep enough n overflows any stack.
func depth(n int) int {
    if n == 0 {
        return 0
    }
    return depth(n - 1) + 1
}

component page ui.node {
    ui.text(value="page")
}

ui.window {
    page()
}

func testAFirstTestPasses(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.assert(depth(3) == 3)
}

func testTheProgramGoesAway(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.assert(depth(1000000000) > 0)
}
-- testrun/android/kotlin/app.sngl/page/1 --
sha256:492f5232dbb348a23d0afc99e15b3e6f
{
  "results": [
    {
      "Desc": "AFirstTestPasses",
      "Passed": true
    },
    {
      "Desc": "TheProgramGoesAway",
      "Log": [
        "exception: StackOverflowError: null"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
